payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Are the scene's principal shapes and meaningful internal boundaries represented with convincing pencil-like contour linework?
node.criteria: Pass if pencil-like contour strokes broadly describe the principal forms and meaningful internal boundaries across the scene. Evidence may include fine irregular graphite-like lines, sketch-like stroke articulation or variable line weight. Contours may follow the source image's boundaries: preserving their geometry does not disqualify a pencil-drawn rendering. Every boundary need not be outlined, and some soft edges may remain. Fail if the principal boundaries still appear photographic or merely sharpened, without broadly convincing drawn linework. Reduced saturation, uniform grain and stronger photographic edges alone do not satisfy this condition. Assess contour appearance independently of interior shading. Use unknown only when visual evidence is insufficient to establish the contour style.
node.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images against the requested pencil-drawing transformation. Independently judge this contour condition as pass, fail or unknown. Inspect the plate rim, potato-slice perimeters and internal marks, carrot boundaries, fork tines, and glass and pitcher outlines. Ground the judgment in the visible character and distribution of boundary strokes: identify where irregular graphite-like articulation, sketch strokes or variable line weight represent forms, and distinguish those features from photographic edge contrast, softened edges or sharpening halos. Use corresponding source boundaries to distinguish drawn representation from retained photographic edges; unchanged geometry is not evidence against pencil contours. Neither desaturation and grain nor incomplete interior shading determines this judgment. Cite concrete boundaries supporting the assessment rather than inferring linework from the overall stylized appearance. Use unknown only if the visual evidence cannot establish contour character or extent, not merely because confidence is low or assessments disagree. The target is pencil-drawn representation of the image's visual content; the reference is the supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image is desaturated and grainy, but the plate rim, potato-slice edges, carrot boundaries, fork tines, and glass and pitcher outlines mostly retain smooth photographic edge contrast. They do not show broadly convincing irregular graphite-like contour strokes or variable line weight; the grain does not establish drawn linework.

d1_shading_modeling: The node’s evidence supports a tonal-modeling failure, but that single failure should not be treated as proof that the requested edit made no progress: the edited image is visibly desaturated and has softened, grainy, pencil-like surface treatment, while retaining substantial photographic gradients and reflective highlights. Keep this criterion narrowly focused on whether tonal modeling itself reads as graphite, and distinguish smooth rubbed graphite from photographic shading by examining material cues and how values articulate form—not smoothness alone. Record both converted-looking regions and substantial retained-photo regions, and avoid letting the latter erase partial progress elsewhere. The aggregate `no` versus reference `partial` suggests a routing/criterion-coverage issue: this node assesses only tonal modeling, so ensure the overall decision can combine its failure with evidence from other requested transformation dimensions. Do not force a pass or weaken the criterion; preserve `unknown` for genuinely inadequate visual evidence, not disagreement or uncertainty. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
d1_shading_marks: The fail is plausible for this narrowly defined surface-mark check: the edit is desaturated and grainy, while many food and glass surfaces retain photographic detail. But the binding should make the node report localized evidence and extent rather than letting that broad failure imply that no requested change occurred. In the edited image, for example, the potato and vegetable surfaces have softened, mottled graphite-like texture, while the plate, tablecloth, and glassware still show substantial photographic shading and reflections. Ask the judge to compare corresponding source and edited regions, distinguish newly introduced drawing-like texture from source texture or uniform noise, and state which major regions support or contradict the criterion. Keep the pass threshold intact: partial-looking treatment need not pass if convincing marks are not established across major surfaces. Ensure this node’s result remains one dimension in the aggregate, so its fail does not erase progress on other dimensions of the pencil-drawing request. The trace is valid and has no transport, schema, or dependency failure; low confidence or disagreement alone would not justify unknown.
